title: Samosa
howToPrepare:
Ingredients:

   For the Dough:

   2 cups all-purpose flour

   ¼ cup oil or melted ghee

   ½ tsp salt

   ½ cup water (add gradually for a stiff dough)

   For the Potato Filling:

   4 medium potatoes (boiled, peeled, and coarsely mashed)

   ½ cup green peas (boiled or frozen)

   1 tbsp oil or ghee

   1 tsp cumin seeds1 tbsp ginger (minced or paste)

   1 to 2 green chilies (chopped)

   1 tsp coriander powder1 tsp garam masala

   1 tsp amchur (dry mango powder)

   Salt to taste

   Instructions:

   1. Make the Dough-

   Mix the flour, salt, and oil (or ghee) together in a large bowl.
   Rub the oil into the flour with your fingers until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
   Add water slowly to knead a very stiff, firm dough.Cover the dough with a damp cloth and let it rest for 30 to 40 minutes.

   2. Prepare the Filling-

    Heat oil in a pan over medium heat, then add the cumin seeds and let them crackle.
    Stir in the minced ginger and chopped green chilies.Add the mashed potatoes, green peas, coriander powder, garam masala, amchur powder, and salt.
    Mix well and cook for a few minutes, then let the filling cool completely before shaping.

    3. Shape the Samosas-

    Divide the rested dough into equal portions and roll each into a thin circle.
    Cut the circle in half to create two semi-circles.
    Brush a little water along the straight cut edge.
    Fold the edges together to form a tight cone, pinching the seam to seal.
    Spoon the cooled potato filling into the cone.
    Apply water to the open top edge and press firmly to seal it closed into a triangle.

    4. Fry the Samosas-

    Heat oil in a deep pan over medium-low heat.
    Carefully drop the assembled samosas into the warm oil.
    Fry them slowly on medium-low heat for 8 to 12 minutes, turning occasionally, until they turn deep golden brown and crispy.
    Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
